summary: Fourteen days of high-quality CGM data show an average glucose of 121.6 mg/dL, 86.0% time in range, 8.9% above range, and 5.1% below range. Hypoglycemia is the main safety constraint, particularly overnight and around 18:00-19:00 local time. Afternoon hyperglycemia is often followed by substantial insulin on board and later declines, but absent meal, carbohydrate, activity, and rescue-treatment records prevent separation of profile settings from UAM, SMB, Dynamic ISF, corrections, and food absorption. No profile or AAPS parameter change has enough isolated evidence; the primary action is to keep the current profile while obtaining one controlled, fully documented overnight observation before reviewing automation and meal strategy sequentially.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage and cadence support broad pattern analysis. The authoritative top-level AAPS profile is complete, and profile_context declares it historically applicable. Treatment and loop telemetry are substantial, but causal reconstruction is limited by absent carbohydrate entries and representative rather than exhaustive response records.
analysis_steps.evidence: There are 3,995 valid CGM readings, 98.7% coverage, an estimated five-minute cadence, no invalid or duplicate readings, ten gaps, and a largest gap of 65 minutes. The package includes 2,315 treatments, 655 insulin entries, 6,214 device-status records, all profile segments, and all six AAPS decision groups.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Basal assessment requires fasting-like windows. CR, meal timing, and absorption assessment require meal-linked records. Correction assessment requires total IOB, SMB, and temporary-basal context.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No entered carbohydrate, meal composition, activity, rescue-carbohydrate, or symptom records are available. Supplied therapy-response and treatment lists are representative subsets.

analysis_steps.findings: Hypoglycemia is the leading safety constraint despite strong overall time in range. Recurrent overnight and early-evening lows limit any proposal that would increase insulin exposure. Hyperglycemia is episodic and concentrated mainly in the afternoon.
analysis_steps.evidence: Average glucose is 121.6 mg/dL, time in range 86.0%, time below range 5.1%, SD 39.7 mg/dL, and CV 32.6%. Confirmed readings reached 41-42 mg/dL. Local TBR was 18.5% at 01:00 and 15.3% at 19:00. Local TAR reached 32.1% at 16:00. Daily TBR reached 12.8% on 18 August.
analysis_steps.dependencies: All later assessments must distinguish basal insulin from residual IOB, corrections, SMB, Dynamic ISF, food absorption, temporary targets, and activity.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: There is no finger-stick confirmation, symptom record, low-treatment record, or activity record for individual severe-low episodes.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight and 18:00-19:00 low patterns merit verification, but they are not proven basal defects. The 04:00-08:00 aggregate is comparatively stable apart from an isolated severe reading. Daytime and afternoon rises cannot be attributed to inadequate basal because meals are unrecorded and automation frequently changes delivery. The 90 mg/dL overnight target provides limited margin during IOB-associated declines, but a target change is not isolated by the available data.
analysis_steps.evidence: Local TBR is 11.4% at 00:00, 18.5% at 01:00, 10.1% at 02:00, 10.2% at 03:00, and 15.3% at 19:00. Local 04:00-08:00 averages are approximately 99.5-110.5 mg/dL with lower TBR. Loop records include repeated zero or reduced temporary basal when lows were predicted, showing that outcomes reflect profile settings plus automation and IOB.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Overnight interpretation depends on finding a period without a late meal, correction, activity, rescue carbohydrate, temporary target, or substantial starting IOB. Evening interpretation depends on the preceding meal and automated-insulin sequence.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No verified fasting windows or complete meal, activity, and rescue-treatment context are available.

analysis_steps.findings: No CR segment can be tested without meal amounts and timing. The fixed ISF of 56 mg/dL/U cannot be isolated because Dynamic ISF, SMB, temporary basal, and pre-existing IOB materially affect corrections. Large late declines do not support shortening the 10-hour DIA.
analysis_steps.evidence: All 24 therapy-response windows are labelled Correction Bolus and show highly variable responses through six hours. Several reach 47-69 mg/dL two to four hours later, while other windows rise initially. Representative variable sensitivity spans roughly 28-124 mg/dL/U versus the fixed ISF of 56 mg/dL/U.
analysis_steps.dependencies: CR requires matched meal and bolus records. ISF requires a correction without food, activity, or additional automated insulin. DIA requires complete delivery history and observation after insulin delivery stops.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: There are no meal-linked carbohydrate amounts, prebolus intervals, immediate bolus percentages, or isolated correction tests.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are functioning with adequate CGM data. With COB consistently zero, UAM is the main mechanism responding to unannounced rises. Always-enabled SMB plus UAM can accumulate insulin during prolonged rises, but the data do not isolate either feature as the cause of severe lows. Increasing SMB eligibility, frequency, or limits is unsupported.
analysis_steps.evidence: SMB and UAM are enabled, SMB is always enabled, and representative loop records repeatedly report COB 0. Sampled IOB reached approximately 4.73 U and 5.94 U during hyperglycemia, while other loop records later predicted very low glucose and reduced basal.
analysis_steps.dependencies: SMB/UAM behavior depends on basal, target, fixed and dynamic sensitivity, DIA, SMB limits, meal announcements, and manual corrections.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: There is no exhaustive SMB sequence linked to documented meals, corrections, activity, and subsequent glucose.

analysis_steps.findings: Dynamic ISF is the leading automation-level explanation for more aggressive dosing during hyperglycemia, but it remains confounded by unannounced food and repeated insulin delivery. Autosens is disabled; sensitivity_ratio values of 1 are neutral adjustments and were not interpreted as Autosens status. Maximum basal and maximum IOB are permissive ceilings, but concentration context and actual lower operational limits prevent deriving safe replacement values.
analysis_steps.evidence: Dynamic ISF is enabled at 70%, and variable sensitivity fell to approximately 42.5, 37.9, and 27.8 mg/dL/U during selected highs. Maximum basal is 12 U/h versus scheduled basal of 0.5-0.8 U/h, and maximum IOB is 25 U. Representative suggested rates were often capped below 12 U/h.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Dynamic ISF should be assessed before changing fixed ISF, CR, basal, or SMB limits. Safety ceilings require confirmation of insulin concentration, pump configuration, and intended safety rationale.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: The package does not establish the complete sensitivity and insulin-delivery sequence for every low or fully clarify the operational implications of the profile name referring to dilution.

analysis_steps.findings: The declared analysis context contains no typical meal strategy, so no numeric prebolus interval or immediate bolus percentage can be reproduced. Observed execution shows reactive correction and automated delivery with no entered carbohydrates. The afternoon-high/evening-low pattern does not support adding more upfront insulin or strengthening CR without matched meal evidence.
analysis_steps.evidence: The declared meal_strategies list is empty, strategy_stable_for_period is null, treatment_summary contains zero carbohydrate entries, and all supplied response windows are correction events. Local TAR is highest from 14:00-17:00, followed by increased TBR around 18:00-19:00.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Meal assessment depends on actual carbohydrate amount, prebolus timing, immediate bolus percentage, CR, starting glucose, target, IOB, SMB/UAM, Dynamic ISF, temporary targets, and six-hour response.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Prebolus minutes, immediate bolus percentage, meal carbohydrate amounts, and per-meal execution records are absent.

analysis_steps.findings: No regular carbohydrate or e-carb entry is available, so e-carb amount, start offset, duration, and glucose action cannot be assessed. Prolonged rises cannot be attributed to delayed absorption without separating meal, IOB, SMB, temporary-target, correction, and activity effects.
analysis_steps.evidence: carb_treatment_entries is empty, total entered carbohydrates are 0 g, extended carbohydrate entries are zero, average extended-carbohydrate duration is null, and representative loop records report COB 0.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Assessment requires a meal-linked carbohydrate or e-carb entry and complete glucose and insulin response through six hours.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: E-carb amount, timestamp, start offset, duration, meal composition, and matched six-hour response are absent.

analysis_steps.findings: The evidence supports a safe sequence rather than an immediate setting change. First preserve the authoritative profile and verify the overnight low pattern under a naturally occurring, well-documented low-confounding window. Second review Dynamic ISF, SMB/UAM exposure, and safety ceilings using complete delivery context. Third evaluate meal timing, immediate bolus delivery, CR, and e-carbs from one fully documented recurring meal. No dependent parameters should change together.
analysis_steps.evidence: High-quality CGM confirms recurrent hypoglycemia, but zero carb entries and variable correction responses prevent causal attribution. Afternoon highs coexist with substantial automated IOB and later lows. Every decision-inventory value is present, so unsupported AAPS changes are recorded as keep rather than verify.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Any future setting proposal depends on confirming insulin concentration and profile configuration, validating low readings, and obtaining an observation that isolates the parameter being reviewed.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: The most important unresolved evidence is one complete overnight window and one complete recurring-meal record with meal, bolus, automation, IOB, activity, and six-hour glucose context.

strengths: CGM data quality is good, with 98.7% coverage, no invalid readings, and no duplicates.
Overall time in range is strong at 86.0%, with an average glucose of 121.6 mg/dL.
The authoritative profile contains complete basal, CR, ISF, target, DIA, SMB/UAM, sensitivity, limit, and absorption settings.
The loop frequently reduced or stopped temporary basal when low glucose was predicted, demonstrating active protective responses.
The 04:00-08:00 local-time aggregate is comparatively stable and does not show a broad recurring high pattern.
issues: Time below range is 5.1%, with confirmed readings as low as 41-42 mg/dL and recurring risk overnight and around 18:00-19:00 local time.

Afternoon hyperglycemia is followed by later declines and sometimes substantial IOB, creating a risk that profile insulin, Dynamic ISF, SMB/UAM, and corrections are addressing the same rise before absorption ends.
No carbohydrate entries, meal records, activity records, or low-treatment records are available, preventing reliable separation of basal, CR, meal timing, absorption, and automation effects.
Dynamic ISF produced much stronger effective sensitivity during selected highs than the fixed profile ISF, but its independent contribution to later lows remains unresolved.

Maximum basal of 12 U/h and maximum IOB of 25 U are permissive relative to the scheduled basal and observed low risk, although actual delivery was often constrained below those ceilings and the package does not support replacement values.

recommendations.title: Keep the profile and verify the overnight pattern first
recommendations.description: The overnight low pattern is real, but late IOB, corrections, meals, activity, and rescue carbohydrates remain plausible explanations. Changing basal or target before separating these factors could worsen another time period.

suggested_change.scope: All current basal, target, CR, ISF, and DIA values
suggested_change.next_action: Review one naturally occurring overnight interval with no late meal, correction, temporary target, unusual activity, or substantial starting IOB, while recording CGM validation and all insulin delivery.

recommendations.title: Review automation only after the profile observation
recommendations.description: Dynamic ISF, always-enabled SMB, UAM, and repeated automated delivery can produce substantial IOB during unannounced rises. The current evidence supports no increase and no simultaneous automation changes.

suggested_change.next_action: After the overnight review, inspect one complete high-to-low sequence for variable sensitivity, SMBs, temporary basal, manual corrections, IOB, temporary targets, and insulin concentration before considering one automation change.

recommendations.title: Document one recurring meal before changing meal settings
recommendations.description: The package contains no declared or observed numeric prebolus, immediate bolus percentage, carbohydrate amount, or e-carb strategy. Afternoon highs followed by evening lows do not support adding more upfront insulin without meal-linked evidence.

suggested_change.scope: Prebolus, immediate bolus percentage, CR, SMB/UAM interaction, and e-carbs
suggested_change.next_action: Capture one recurring meal with carbohydrate amount, actual timing, actual immediate percentage, any e-carb details, starting IOB, all automated delivery, activity, and glucose through six hours.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep the current basal schedule and the rest of the profile unchanged for now, and use one fully documented naturally occurring overnight interval to verify whether glucose falls without late food, correction insulin, unusual activity, temporary targets, or substantial starting IOB.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Overnight TBR is elevated and severe lows occurred, but automation and residual IOB materially affect observed glucose. Daytime highs are also confounded by absent meal records. No individual basal, target, CR, ISF, or DIA value has isolated evidence sufficient for a supported old-to-new change.
profile_recommendation.next_check: For one overnight interval, record glucose confirmation, starting IOB, all basal and SMB delivery, last meal and correction times, temporary targets, activity, and any low treatment, then assess whether a reproducible fall begins before each relevant basal segment.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Overnight TBR is elevated, but late corrections, starting IOB, automated delivery, and unrecorded food or low treatment remain unresolved. A clean overnight observation is required before attributing the pattern to this segment.

The local 04:00-06:00 aggregate is comparatively stable. An isolated severe morning reading does not establish a recurring defect, and assessment depends on IOB, activity, sensor validation, and preceding insulin.
Local 06:00-08:00 data are mostly in range, while the isolated 42 mg/dL reading lacks complete IOB, activity, and confirmation context. No supported replacement value can be derived.
Glucose rises during this broad segment, but meals are unrecorded and UAM, SMB, corrections, and temporary basal are active. Increasing basal could worsen the later 18:00-19:00 low pattern.

This segment starts during the highest average-glucose period but is followed by a sharp decline and increased evening TBR. Meal absorption and accumulated automated IOB are stronger competing explanations than isolated basal deficiency.
Low risk increases during this segment, but preceding afternoon corrections, SMB, Dynamic ISF, and activity are unresolved. A segment change requires an observation without those dependencies.

Local 19:00 TBR is 15.3%, creating concern, but the hour commonly follows afternoon hyperglycemia and insulin accumulation. The data do not isolate the scheduled basal or support a concrete replacement.
No meal carbohydrate amount, bolus timing, or immediate bolus percentage is available for this interval. CR cannot be separated from basal, IOB, ISF, DIA, SMB/UAM, and unrecorded intake.
The early-morning aggregate is relatively stable, and there are no matched meal records to test this CR. Any change would be unsupported and dependent on actual meal timing and automation.
Morning and afternoon rises could reflect meal timing, amount, absorption, or UAM rather than this CR. Later low risk argues against strengthening it without a matched six-hour meal record.

Afternoon highs are followed by evening lows, and no meal-linked carbohydrate or bolus data are available. Strengthening this CR could add insulin to an interval already affected by SMB, Dynamic ISF, and corrections.
Late-evening and overnight low risk constrains additional insulin, while no matched meal evidence tests this CR. Basal, target, IOB, and meal effects remain unresolved.

Correction responses are highly variable and include additional automated insulin. Dynamic ISF frequently changes effective sensitivity, so the fixed ISF cannot be isolated and should not change together with automation.

The target may provide limited margin during overnight IOB-associated declines, but the data do not separate target effects from basal, late insulin, and low treatment. A concrete new target is unsupported.
Afternoon highs do not establish that this target is too high because meals are unrecorded and automation produces substantial IOB. Lowering it could worsen the later low pattern.
Late-evening TBR is elevated, but residual IOB, corrections, and unrecorded food or low treatment remain plausible. The target should be assessed only after a documented overnight observation.

Several glucose declines occur two to six hours after corrections, so shortening DIA is unsupported and could hide active insulin. Complete delivery history is required to determine whether 10 hours overstates the action tail.

Both features are active with good CGM coverage and provide responses to unannounced rises. Severe lows and high IOB prevent any increase, but absent meal and complete delivery records do not isolate SMB or UAM as independently defective.

Always-enabled SMB is materially relevant with zero entered carbs, but no activation switch can be linked independently to the lows. Changing activation while also assessing Dynamic ISF, CR, or meal timing would confound the result.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: The configured interval and limits are present, and severe lows argue against increasing exposure. Representative rather than exhaustive SMB data cannot identify which component should change or support concrete replacement values.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS maximum basal and maximum IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: These ceilings are permissive relative to scheduled basal and observed IOB, creating a material review concern. However, actual delivery was often constrained below them, and insulin concentration and configuration context are insufficient to derive supported replacement values.

Dynamic ISF is the leading automation-level explanation for aggressive correction during highs, with variable sensitivity substantially below the fixed ISF in selected episodes. Unannounced food, SMB, temporary basal, and corrections remain confounders, so no isolated new value is supported.
There are no entered carbohydrates or COB trajectories, so neither absorption component can be tested. Meal-linked data are required before attributing prolonged rises to these settings.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Keep any existing prebolus timing and immediate bolus percentage unchanged because no declared numeric values are present in the package; keep SMB/UAM settings unchanged while documenting their actual delivery; and do not introduce or alter e-carbs without a meal-linked amount, start offset, duration, and six-hour response.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Observed execution contains no carb entries and mainly shows UAM, SMB, temporary basal, and corrections responding to rises. Afternoon hyperglycemia is followed by increased evening low risk, so adding more immediate insulin, strengthening CR, or modelling delayed carbs without matched evidence could increase insulin accumulation.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Capture one recurring meal with timestamp, carbohydrate amount, actual prebolus minutes, actual immediate bolus percentage, any e-carb amount, start offset and duration, starting glucose and IOB, all SMB and temporary-basal delivery, temporary targets, activity, corrections, and glucose through six hours.

exceptions.pattern: Recurring local 14:00-17:00 elevation followed by increased low risk around 18:00-19:00
exceptions.suggestion: Use this as the first fully documented meal observation and avoid interpreting the rise alone as evidence for more basal or more immediate meal insulin.
exceptions.rationale: TAR reaches 22.6-32.1% from 14:00-17:00, while local 19:00 TBR is 15.3% and sampled afternoon correction windows sometimes reach 47-56 mg/dL later.

implementation_steps: Confirm that the selected top-level profile, insulin concentration, pump configuration, and displayed units match the intended setup; profile_context already declares this profile applicable to the analysis period.
Validate severe or unexpected CGM lows with the user's established glucose-confirmation process and preserve records of symptoms and low treatment.

Keep current profile and AAPS decision-inventory values unchanged while reviewing one naturally occurring overnight interval with complete IOB, insulin delivery, meal, correction, temporary-target, activity, and low-treatment context.

If the overnight observation does not isolate a profile issue, review one complete afternoon high-to-evening low sequence for Dynamic ISF, variable sensitivity, SMBs, UAM, temporary basal, manual corrections, IOB, and safety ceilings.
Review only one dependent setting at a time if later evidence supports a concrete old-to-new value, then monitor glucose closely before considering another setting.
After profile and automation review, capture one fully documented recurring meal for six hours before evaluating CR, prebolus timing, immediate bolus percentage, or e-carbs.
education: Hourly glucose averages combine meals, corrections, activity, temporary targets, and automated delivery; they do not by themselves identify an incorrect basal or CR segment.
A lower ISF value in mg/dL/U represents a stronger correction effect. Dynamic ISF can therefore make dosing more aggressive during hyperglycemia even when the fixed profile ISF is unchanged.
UAM interprets glucose patterns without entered COB; it is not automatic duplicate counting of COB.
A sensitivity_ratio of 1 is a neutral current adjustment and does not mean Autosens is enabled.
E-carbs describe expected carbohydrate absorption and are not the same as a pump extended bolus.
A long DIA preserves recognition of residual insulin. Shortening it without action-tail evidence can make active insulin appear to have ended sooner.
Safety ceilings such as maximum basal and maximum IOB do not optimize routine dosing; they define how far automation may go when other conditions request insulin.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only and does not provide medical advice.
Every proposed future change must be independently verified, made one at a time, and followed by close glucose monitoring.
No AAPS setting should be changed automatically from this analysis.
Confirmed or suspected severe hypoglycemia, recurrent unexplained lows, pump occlusion, or pump error warrants prompt use of the user's established safety plan and appropriate professional support.
The documented time below range and readings of 41-42 mg/dL make avoidance of additional insulin exposure the primary constraint until the low patterns are better explained.
